Description: Displays the current revision of the system BIOS firmware.
The Service Tag is the system's serial number that uniquely identifies the Dell system.

An Asset Tag is a string of 0 to 64 characters in length that can be used by an IT administrator to uniquely identify a particular system. NOTE: Some systems may support maximum length of an asset tag as 10 or 12 characters.
The Ownership Tag is a string of 0 to 80 characters in length that can be used by a user/customer to display a system-specific message on the BIOS start-up and setup screens.
Displays the system manufacture date (mmddyyyy).
This field displays the date (mmddyyyy) the system was first powered-on after leaving the factory.
The Express Service Code is a mathematical hash applied to the service tag. The Express Service Code is seen in BIOS Setup and on an exterior sticker (customer systems).
Displays the amount of main memory physically installed in the system.

Displays the amount of main memory available to the operating system. NOTE: Due to an amount of memory being assigned for the system use, Memory Available is less then Memory Installed. Note that certain operating system may not be able to use all the available memory.
Displays the technology of the main memory installed in the system.
Displays the amount of main memory physically installed in the DIMM slot A.
Displays the amount of main memory physically installed in the DIMM slot B.
Displays the amount of main memory physically installed in the DIMM slot C.
Displays the amount of main memory physically installed in the DIMM slot D.

Boot List option determines the boot mode of the system. Uefi - Enables booting to Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) capable operating systems. Legacy (the default) - Ensures compatibility with OSes that do not support UEFI. NOTE: Legacy boot mode is not allowed when secure boot is enabled or Legacy Option ROM is disabled.

Specifies the order in which a system searches for devices when trying to find an operating system to boot. The Boot Sequence option allows users to customize the boot order and boot ability of boot devices. The UEFI BIOS allows the selection of UEFI boot paths or Legacy boot devices.

UefiBootPathSecurity determines whether the system must prompt you to enter the Admin password. This occurs when the UefiBootPathSecurity is set while booting from a UEFI boot path (from the F12 Boot Menu).
AlwaysExceptInternalHddPxe - All UEFI boot paths require the Admin password, except for boot paths hosted on internal hard disk drives or PXE Boot.
AlwaysExceptInternalHdd - All UEFI boot paths requires the Admin password, except for the boot paths that are hosted on an internal hard disk drive.
Always - Booting from any UEFI boot path requires the Admin password.
Never - The Admin password is not required for booting from UEFI boot paths.
Enabling BIOS Setup Advanced Mode will make all BIOS settings visible.
Enables or disables the LED status of Microphone.

This option is disabled by default. If enabled, UEFI Networking Protocols are installed/available, allowing pre-OS and early OS networking features to use the enabled NICs. This option may be used without turning on PXE.

Configures the operating mode of the integrated SATA hard drive controller. Disabled - The SATA controllers are hidden. Ata - SATA is configured for ATA mode. Ahci - SATA is configured for AHCI mode. Raid - SATA is configured to support RAID mode (Intel Rapid Restore Technology).
Controls whether hard drive errors for integrated drives are reported during system startup.

Configures the USB PowerShare feature behavior. Enabled - Charges the external devices, such as phones and portable music players, using the stored system battery when the system is turned off or in sleep mode. This feature works only if  (1) The device is connected through the USB Powershare port on the notebook. (2) The system is connected with AC power. (3) The battery charge is above 50 percent. Disabled - Turns this feature off and devices attached to the USB PowerShare port will not be charged when the system is in a sleep mode or turned off.
Enables or disables the integrated audio controller.
Enables or disables the built-in speaker.
Enables or disables the internal or external microphone.

Configures the the keyboard illumination brightness percentage. The keyboard automatically illuminates when the internal keyboard, touchpad or pointstick are used. Off - Turns the keyboard illumination off. Brightness levels - Specify the percentage (25, 50, 75, 100) to adjust the brightness level. Auto - Keyboard illumination is automatically adjusted based on ambience light leavel. NOTE - Auto option requires ambience light sensor that may not be available on all systems.

Enables or disables the toggling light emissions using hotkey Fn+B. Enabled - Pressing Fn+B will toggle light emissions from the system. Disabled - Pressing Fn+B keys has no effect and will not toggle light emissions from the system.
Enables or disables M2 PCIE SSD 0

Configures the timeout value for the keyboard backlight when the system is running only on battery power. Possible values are: 5s - Keyboard backlight stays on for 5 seconds. 10s - Keyboard backlight stays on for 10 seconds. 15s - Keyboard backlight stays on for 15 seconds. 30s - Keyboard backlight stays on for 30 seconds. 1m - Keyboard backlight stays on for 1 minute. 5m - Keyboard backlight stays on for 5 minutes. 15m - Keyboard backlight stays on for 15 minutes. Never - keyboard backlight always stays on.

Configures the timeout value for the keyboard backlight when an AC adapter is plugged into the system. Possible values are: 5s - Keyboard backlight stays on for 5 seconds. 10s - Keyboard backlight stays on for 10 seconds. 15s - Keyboard backlight stays on for 15 seconds. 30s - Keyboard backlight stays on for 30 seconds. 1m - Keyboard backlight stays on for 1 minute. 5m - Keyboard backlight stays on for 5 minutes. 15m - Keyboard backlight stays on for 15 minutes. Never - keyboard backlight always stays on.
Enables or disables the camera.

If Boot Support is enabled, the system allows to boot any type of USB Mass Storage devices( hard drive, memory key or floppy). USB-aware OS always see USB Mass Storage devices irrespective of this setting, provided the port is enabled.

Enabled - Devices attached to this USB port is enabled and available in the operating system. Disabled - Devices attached to this USB port is disabled and not visible in the operating system. NOTE: USB mouse and keyboard will work even if the External USB Port is disabled.
Enables or disables the thunderbolt controller in system.
Enables or disables booting from the Thunderbolt device.
Enables OROMs and pre-boot UEFI drivers provided by Thunderbolt devices or PCIe devices.
Sets the panel brightness to be used when the system is using battery power only. 0 means panel brightness will be 0% and 15 means panel brightness will be 100%.
Sets the panel brightness to be used when the system is using AC power. 0 means panel brightness will be 0% and 15 means panel brightness will be 100%.

Sets the value to the Absolute interface and control the Absolute service using the following options: Enabled - The Absolute interface is enabled. The Absolute service may now be activated or deactivated. Disabled - The Absolute interface is disabled. The Absolute service does not run. PermanentlyDisabled - The Absolute interface is disabled, and can only be enabled using a full reset at the factory.

Enables or disables the additional UEFI SMM Security Mitigation protections. The operating system uses this feature to protect the secure environment created by virtualization based security. Enabling this feature provides the additional UEFI SMM Security Mitigation protections support. However, this feature may cause compatibility or functionality issues with some legacy tools and applications.

Determines whether the changes to the system and HDD passwords are permitted or restricted if an admin password is set.

Disabled - If disabled, then the system and HDD passwords are locked by admin password and cannot be set, modified, or deleted unless Admin password is provided.
Enabled - If enabled, then the system and the HDD passwords can be set, modified, or deleted.

Enables or disables BIOS updates via UEFI capsule update packages.

NOTE: Disabling this option blocks the BIOS updates from services such as Microsoft Windows Update and Linux Vender Firmware Service (LVFS).
Specifies if System Password has been set.
Specifies if Admin Password has been set.

Displays the details of each HDD. The following information is displayed: (1) HDDName: The name of the HDD. (2) Present: Whether the HDD is physically present. (3) PwdProtected: Whether a password exists for the HDD. (4) PendingRestart: Whether reboot is pending to set the password. (5) AdminOnlyChange: Whether the changes to the password can be made only by an administrator. (6) SecureEraseSupported: Whether HDD Secure Erase is supported (7) SecureEraseEnabled: Whether HDD Secure Erase is enabled.
Sets, changes or clears the administrator (admin) password (also called the setup password). If you delete the admin password, the system password, if set, is also deleted.
Sets, changes or clears the system password (also called as User password). You need to enter the system password, if set, when the system is powered on.
Sets, changes or clears HDD password. Provide the HDD password, if set, when the system is powered on. NOTE: After Setting the HDD password, restart the system to apply the changes.

Enables or disables the enforced use of strong password. If enabled, Admin and System passwords must contain at least one upper case character, at least one lower case character, and must contain minimum eight characters.
Allows users to skip the entry of the System password, internal Hard Disk Drive password, fingerprint scan or smartcard on either/both Reboot (warm boot) or S3 resume (resume from standby).

The Chassis Intrusion switch is a physical switch which triggers an event when the chassis is opened. Enabled - The system detects and reports Chassis Intrusion events to the system display on boot-up. Disabled - The system does not detect and report Chassis Intrusion events to the system display on boot-up. SilentEnable - The system detects but does not report Chassis Intrusion events to the system display on boot-up.

Displays the status of chassis intrusion. NOTE: Except TripReset, all values are read-only. DoorOpen - Indicates that chassis door is open. Tripped - Indicates that the chassis door was opened since the last time the sensor-detection logic was reset. DoorClosed - Indicates that chassis door is closed. TripReset - Resets the sensor-detection logic to detect the next closed-to-open transition on the chassis door.
Enabled - Prevents users from entering Setup when an Admin password is set. Disabled - Allows users to entering Setup even when an Admin password is set.

Enables or disables the master password settings. CAUTION: Using the Dell Command | PowerShell Provider, you cannot disable this feature. Enabled - The master password cannot be used to (1) clear other passwords (2) unlock and access Hard Disk Drive (3) erase data from Hard Disk Drive. Disabled - The master password can be used to (1) clear other passwords (2) unlock and access Hard Disk Drive (3) erase data from Hard Disk Drive. NOTE: One of the methods of configuring this feature is from the BIOS setup screen.

When enabled tpmppiclearoverride, performing the TPM clear command within operating system does not require user's interaction. When disabled, performing the TPM clear command within operating system requires user's interaction.
Note: To set TpmPpiClearOverride, AdminPassword must be set.

Sets the Hash Algorithm used for TPM 2.0 measurements. Disabled - Sets hash algorithm to SHA-1. Enabled - Sets hash algorithm to SHA-256. SHA384 - Sets hash algorithm to SHA-384. SHA512 - Sets hash algorithm to SHA-512. NOTE: This value cannot be changed if TPM is already owned.

Controls whether the Trusted Platform Module (TPM) in the system is enabled and visible to the operating system. Enabled - BIOS will turn on the TPM during POST, and can be used by the operating system. Disabled - BIOS will not turn on the TPM during POST, and the TPM will be non-functional and invisible to the operating system. NOTE: Disabling this option does not change any settings that you may have made to the TPM, nor does it delete or change any information or keys you may have stored there. It simply turns off the TPM so that it cannot be used. When you re-enable this option, TPM will work exactly as it did before it was disabled.

When you enable TPM Clear, the TPM ownership is cleared during the next boot and the system firmware sets the value of TPM Clear to disabled. When you disable TPM Clear, the TPM ownership remains unchanged.

Allows the variation of Secure Boot operation mode. Possible values are Audit Mode and Deployed Mode. Audit Mode enables the evaluation of changes to the Secure Boot key database. Deployed Mode is the normal mode of operation for measuring the UEFI executable images. Attempting the transition to Audit Mode by writing '1' to the DA token may fail if the system is not in OSMM.

Enables or disables the secure boot feature. For secure boot to be enabled, the system needs to be in UEFI boot mode and the Enable Legacy Option ROMs option needs to be turned off. CAUTION: Using the Dell Command | PowerShell Provider, you cannot disable this feature. NOTE: One of the methods of configuring this feature is from the BIOS setup screen.
This field specifies whether the processor will have one or more cores enabled. The performance of some applications will improve with the additional cores.

Intel SpeedStep technology that allows the processor to operate at two or more operating speeds called P-states in ACPI terminology. When disabled, the processor will always operate at its maximum frequency.
Enables or disables additional processor sleep states. The operating system may optionally use these for additional power savings when idle.

Enables or disables the Intel TurboBoost mode of the processor. Disabled - Does not allow the TurboBoost driver to increase the performance state of the processor above the standard performance. Enabled - Allows the Intel Turbo driver to increase the performance of the CPU or graphics processor.
Enables or disables HyperThreading in the processor.

Set the PowerOnLidOpen feature using the following options: Enabled - If this feature is set to enabled, the system powers up from the off state whenever the lid is opened. This system powers on when powered either by the AC adapter or system battery. Disabled - If this feature is set to disabled, the system does not power up from the off state whenever the lid is opened.
Enables or disables the Intel Speed Shift Technology support. Setting this option to Enabled allows the operating system to select the appropriate processor performance automatically.

Configures the days when the system has to turn on automatically at the time specified in AutoOnHour and AutoOnMinute. This function can turn on the system either every day, on weekdays, or on selected days. If AutoOnHour is set to '23', and AutoOnTime is set to '53', then setting AutoOntime to 'Weekdays' will turn on the system automatically on weekdays (Monday to Friday) at 11:53 p.m.. To turn on the system on particular days, set AutoOnTime as 'SelectDays', and then enable or disable individual days by setting AutoOnSunday -enable, AutoOnMonday -disable, etc.
Configures the hour when the system has to turn on automatically. Value ranging from 0-23 can be provided. To set the time 11:59p.m., provide the value as 23.
Configures the minute when the system has to turn on automatically. Value ranging from 0-59 can be provided. To set the time 11:59p.m., provide the value as 59.
Enables or disables the Peak Shift configuration. Using Peak Shift configuration, you can minimize the consumption of AC power during the peak power usage period of the day.
Sets the value of Peak Shift battery threshold. The acceptable value range is from 15 to 100 percentage. When the Peak Shift battery threshold level is reached, the system starts using AC power.

Configures the days settings based on StartTime, EndTime, and ChargeStartTime. Using Peak Shift configuration, you can minimize the consumption of AC power during the peak power usage period of the day. You can set a start and end times for the Peak Shift period. During this period, the system runs on battery if the battery charge is above the set battery threshold value. After the Peak Shift period, the system runs on AC power without charging the battery. The system functions normally using AC power and recharging the battery after the specified ChargeStartTime.
Enables or disables the Advanced Battery Charge Configuration. During working hours, with Advanced Battery Charge Configuration, the batteries can be charged faster using ExpressCharge.

Configures the days settings based on Beginningofday and Workperiod. Advanced Battery charge mode uses standard charging algorithm and other methods during working hours to maximize battery health. During working hours, express charge is used to charge the batteries faster. You can configure the days and the time period during which the battery has to be charged. To enable advanced battery charging, provide the day, start time, and the workperiod.
Controls the system's behavior when AC power is restored after AC power was lost. Disabled - System stays off after AC power is restored. Enabled - System powers on after AC power is restored.
Enabled - Disables the WLAN radio when the system is connected to wire network. When disconnected from the wired network, WLAN radio will be re-enabled.

Enables the system to turn on from the off state when triggered by a special LAN signal, or from the hibernate state when triggered by a special wireless LAN signal. Disabled - Does not allow the system to power on by special LAN signals when it receives a wakeup signal from the LAN or wireless LAN. LanOnly - Allows the system to be powered on by special LAN signals. WlanOnly - Allows the system to be powered on by special WLAN signals. LanWlan - Allows the system to be powered on by special LAN or wireless LAN signals. LanWithPxeBoot - Allows the system to be powered on by special LAN signals and immediately boot to PXE. AddInCard - Allows the system to be powered on by NICs, plugged into the special power connector. Onboard - Allows the system to be powered on by Onboard NIC. SfpNic - Allows the system to wake-up by special SFP signals. LanOrSfpNic - Allows the system to wake-up either by LAN, or by SFP signals. SfpNicWithPxeBoot - Allows the system to wake-up by SFP signals, and immediately boot to PXE.

Blocks the system entering to sleep (S3 state) mode in OS environment. When enabled, the system will not go to sleep mode, Intel Rapid Start will be disabled automatically and OS Power option will be blank if it was set to Sleep earlier.

Configures the primary battery charge mode. The selected charging mode applies to all batteries installed in the system. Auto - Battery settings are adaptively optimized based on your typical battery usage pattern. Standard - Charges the battery at a standard rate. Express - Charges the battery faster using the express charging algorithm, Dell's fast charging technology. PrimAcUse - Charges the battery while plugged-in, preferred for the users who operate their system while plugged in to an external power source. Custom - The battery charging starts and stops based on user settings specified in Primary Battery Custom Charge Start and Primary Battery Custom Charge End.

Sets the percentage value ranging from 50 to 95 at which the custom battery charging should start. NOTE: Primary Battery Custom Charge Start percentage must be less than Primary Battery Custom Charge End percentage and the minimum difference between the two must be 5 percentage.

Sets the percentage value ranging from 55 to 100 at which the custom battery charging should stop. NOTE: Primary Battery Custom Charge Start percentage must be less than Primary Battery Custom Charge End percentage and the minimum difference between the two must be 5 percentage.
Enables or disables waking the system when a docking connection is made.
Enables or disables the lid switch functions. Enabled - OS setting determines the display behavior when lid is closed. Disabled - Display will not be affected when lid is closed.
Configures the maximum power for type-C connector. Possible values are: 7.5 Watts and 15 Watts.
This feature replaces the external NIC MAC address (in a supported dock or dongle) with the selected MAC address from the system. The default value is the System Unique MAC Address.
This option allows the system to indicate that, power button has been pressed during POST by turning on the keyboard backlight.

During POST the system continues to boot or pauses when warnings or errors are detected. This feature can be used for the remotely managed systems that does not have a keyboard or a console for the user to respond. PromptWrnErr - System pauses for the user to respond when warnings or errors are detected.
ContWrn - System continues to boot when warnings are detected, but pauses for the user to respond when errors are detected. ContWrnErr - System continues to boot when warnings or errors are detected.

Enables or disables display of warning messages when you use certain power adapters. The system displays these messages when you attempt to use a power adapter that has too little capacity for your configuration.

This option can speed up the boot process by bypassing some compatibility steps. Minimal - Reduces boot time by skipping certain hardware and configuration initialization during boot. Thorough - Performs complete hardware and configuration initialization during boot. Automatic - Allows the BIOS to decide configuration initialization to be performed during boot. Controls specific steps performed during boot to decrease boot time or increase boot checks.

This option controls the behavior of the Dual function keys, when Fn key is pressed and when it is not. Enabled - <Fn+Esc> key combination toggles the primary behavior of F1 to F12 between their normal and secondary functions. Disabled - You cannot toggle the primary behavior of these keys.
If Enabled, F1 - F12 keys behave as function keys holding Fn key is required to access their secondary functions. Without holding Fn key, the dual function keys behave as normally labeled.
Creates an additional pre-boot delay for specified seconds to allow the user to see POST status messages.
Enables or disables the full screen logo that appears during BIOS POST.\n

Enabled - If Intel Active Management Technology is enabled, MEBx is available through F12 menu and you can provision AMT. MEBx may not be accessible if OROM Keyboard Access is disabled.
RestrictMebxAccess - If Intel Active Management Technology is enabled, MEBx is not available in pre-boot but you can provision AMT from OS.
Disabled - If Intel Active Management Technology is disabled, MEBx is not available in pre-boot. Once disabled, Intel Active Management Technology can only be enabled through BIOS interface. If the Intel AMT is already provisioned, AMT cannot be disabled (Un-provisioning AMT is required to disable AMT).
MEBx stands for Intel Management Engine BIOS Extension. Enables or disables the MEBx hotkey function when the system boots.
Enables or disables the VT technology in applicable CPUs. Trusted execution required for Virtualization technology to be enabled.
Determines whether a Virtual Machine Monitor (VMM) can utilize the additional hardware capabilities provided by Intel Virtualization Technology for Direct IO.

Determines whether a Measured Virtual Machine Monitor (MVMM) can utilize the additional hardware capabilities provided by the Intel Trusted Execution Technology. NOTE: TPM has to be enabled and activated. Also, Virtualization Technology and VT for Direct I/O must be enabled to use this feature.
WWanBusMode sets the interface type of the Wireless Wan (WWAN) card. It is recommended that Microsoft(R) Windows users set this field to PCIe, while all the other users set this to USB.
Enables or disables the internal wireless LAN device.
Enables or disables the internal Bluetooth device.

Enables or disables the system BIOS Recovery option. This feature saves a recovery image to a primary hard disk drive storage, or to an external USB, and uses this recovery image to recover BIOS image when system BIOS fails.

Enabled - BIOS stores the recovery image on a primary hard disk drive storage. So BIOS recovery image is available both from the primary hard disk drive permanent storage as well as via an external USB.
Disabled - BIOS does not store the recovery image on primary hard disk drive storage. So BIOS recovery image is available only via an external USB.

Enables or disables BIOS auto recovery feature. Enabled - If BIOS corruption is detected, the system automatically recovers BIOS without any user interaction. Disabled - Disables BIOS auto recovery feature.

Allows or restricts downgrading of the system BIOS. Enabled - Allows the system to downgrade the system BIOS. Disabled - Restricts the system to downgrade the system BIOS. CAUTION: You cannot enable the Allow BIOS Downgrade feature using the Dell Command | PowerShell Provider. NOTE: One of the methods of enabling the Allow BIOS Downgrade feature is from the BIOS setup screen.
Prevents or allows the BIOS event log to be cleared on the next boot. Keep - Does not clear the BIOS event log on the next boot. Clear - Clears the BIOS event log on the next boot.
Prevents or allows the power event log to be cleared on the next boot. Keep - Does not clear the power event log on the next boot. Clear - Clears the power event log on the next boot.
Prevents or allows the thermal event log to be cleared on the next boot. Keep - Does not clear the thermal event log on the next boot. Clear - Clears the thermal event log on the next boot.
Enables or Disables BIOS Connect feature.
Enables or disables the boot flow for SupportAssist OS recovery tool in the event of certain system errors.\n

Sets the threshold value for auto OS recovery. Possible values: OFF, 1, 2 and 3. Controls the automatic boot flow for SupportAssist System Resolution console and for Dell OS Recovery Tool. The system boots to the SupportAssist System Resolution console and for Dell OS Recovery Tool if, 
the primary operating system fails to boot consecutively. 
		  
the count of boot failure is greater than or equal to the value of the Auto OS Recovery threshold setup option. 
SupportAssist OS Recovery option is enabled.
          
NOTE: If Auto OS Recovery threshold is set to Off, then all automatic boot flow for SupportAssist System Resolution console and for Dell OS Recovery Tool will be disabled.
This feature controls the minimum number of characters that are mandatory for a password.
When enabled, this feature reinforces that the password must contain one lower case letter.
When enabled, this feature reinforces that the password must contain one upper case letter.
When enabled, this feature reinforces that the password must contain one digit number.
When enabled, this feature reinforces password must contain one special character.
When selected, enables Firmware update Over the Air( Remote update of BIOS flash).

This feature controls the type of telemetry for data support.
Disabled - No telemetry.
Basic - Flash and Diags only.
Enhanced - Flash, Diags and Boot Event.
Full - All telemetry.

Reports the type of splash screen logo (Dell or custom) that is passed from BIOS to user. 
Note: You cannot enable or disable this feature using Dell Command | Powershell Provider.
Help text is not available for this feature.
Help text is not available for this feature.

When enabled, if the computer should become unresponsive before completing the BIOSPower-On-Self-Test (POST), the BIOS will attempt to automatically recover the computer.In some cases, this may include reverting BIOS Setup configuration settings to BIOS
default values, and unprovisioning Intel AMT vPro (if applicable).

When the "Block Boot Until Cleared" setting is enabled, you will not be able to boot until returning to this page to clear the warning. If an Admin Password is set, you will need to unlock Setup to clear the warning.

This setting manages whether users can access device configuration screens via hotkeys during system startup. This setting prevents user access to Intel RAID (CTRL+I), LSI RAID (CTRL+C), or Intel Management Engine BIOS Extension (CTRL+P/F12).
Enable = User can access device configuration screens using hotkeys.
One Time Enable = User can access device configuration screens using hotkeys upon the next system startup only. After the next startup, this setting will revert to a disabled state.
Disable = User cannot access device configuration screens using hotkeys.
Enabling Device Configuration Hotkey Access allows users to access device configuration screen by pressing the hotkeys during system startup.
One-Time Enable allows access to device configuration screens via hotkeys only during the next system startup. After the next startup, this setting will revert to a disabled state.
Disabling Device Configuration Hotkey Access will prevent users from accessing Intel RAID (CTRL+I), LSI RAID (CTRL+C), and Intel Management Engine BIOS Extension (CTRL+P/F12).
Disabling USB4 PCIe tunneling may cause the TBT controller to show an error and may cause TBT devices to not function.
This field controls the Firmware Device Tamper Detection feature.
This platform has HTTP(s) Boot capabilities.
Help text is not available for this feature.
When enabled, IPv4 PXE Boot option is available. When disabled, IPv4 PXE Boot option is not available.
When enabled, IPv6 PXE Boot option is available. When disabled, IPv6 PXE Boot option is not available.
This option is used to select the IPv4 and IPv6 option boot order.
When enabled, the system dynamically adjusts voltage and frequencies depending on power and performance requirements.

Total Memory Encryption(TME) is used to protect memory from physical attacks including freeze spray, probing DDR to read the cycles, and others. All of system memory is encrypted by the TME block attached to the memory controller. Up to 16 different encryption keys are supported for use by OS/VMM.

When Enabled, BIOS will notify the OS that the internal ports are not DMA capable. This is intended to help with devices that have OS DMA compatibility issues. This setting does not affect external port DMA or Pre-boot DMA support.

This setting controls Kernel DMA protection for both Internal and External ports.This setting does not directly enable DMA protection in the OS. However, for OS's that support DMA protection, the setting will indicate to the OS that the BIOS supports the feature.

This setting allows the platform administrator to control access via the Legacy Manageability Interface when ABI is enabled and provisioned
Enabled: The Legacy Manageability Interface can be used to read and change BIOS configuration settings
Read-Only: BIOS configuration settings can be read, but cannot be changed through the Legacy Manageability Interface
Disabled: The Legacy Manageability Interface is disabled. BIOS configuration reads and writes are only allowed through ABI
Help text is not available for this feature.

Enable Microsoft UEFI CA(Certificate Authority) will include the UEFI CA in the BIOS UEFI Secure Boot DB database.
When disabled, the Microsoft UEFI CA is removed from the BIOS UEFI Secure Boot DB database.
Disabling the Microsoft UEFI CA could render your system unable to boot. System graphics may not function. Some devices may not function properly. The system could become unrecoverable.
Allow Pre-Boot Modules Only will use the Microsoft UEFI CA to verify the authenticity of option ROMs used for add-in cards.
This setting allows you to change the number of Atom cores available to the OS. The default value is set to the maximum number of Atom cores.

This option controls access to the Physical Security ID (PSID) revert of NVMe hard-drives from the Dell Security Manager prompt. 

When disabled: If a BIOS Admin password is set, PSID revert is protected by the BIOS Admin password and the user will be prompted to enter the BIOS Admin password before performing the revert.
When enabled: PSID revert is allowed to proceed without providing the BIOS Admin password.
Enabling this feature will show the system Ownership Tag in addition to the BIOS Boot logo. This option is only available if an Ownership Tag has been set.
This setting controls Pre-boot DMA protection for both Internal and External ports.

When enabled, if a new PXE boot option is detected, it will be added to the top of the Boot Sequence.
When forced, any PXE boot option will be on the top of the Boot Sequence; and any external PXE boot option(s) have the higher boot priority than any internal PXE boot option(s). OS installation will not change the PXE boot option priority.
This setting allows for cooling fan and processor heat management to adjust system performance, noise and temperature.
This field always allows user to use Audio on Dell Dock external ports.
This field always allows user to use LAN on Dell Dock external ports.

This field always allows user to use connected Type-C Dell Dock to provide data stream when keeping the External USB Ports disabled. When Type-C Dock Override gets enabled, it activates Audio/Lan submenu.

When enabled, Dell OS Agent(s) will be capable of scheduling onboard diagnostics on a subsequent boot which can help assist in the prevention and resolution of hardware related issues.
When disabled, Dell OS Agent(s) will not be capable of scheduling any onboard diagnostics and scans must be initiated manually in the pre-boot environment.
Limits Type-C port functionality to Video or Power only
Help text is not available for this feature.
